source: reconstruction of Yang, Jia & Yan 2023, Fig. 1 (d)
paper_topology: 'the intersection contains two quadrilaterals sharing one edge. The two surfaces are in contact along the common edge of the two quadrilaterals, and intersect transversely at the other six curved edges of the two quadrilaterals, which are also the boundaries of the surfaces'
matched: topology: 6 transversal boundary edges + 1 tangential interior edge (D has a double zero), one connected network, the shared edge shorter than the outer edges; appearance, refitted to the 600 dpi panels: an S-wave ribbon with curled ends and a bump across, the network matching the paper's (Ours row) to ~0.2 / 2.3 px; camera orthographic el 20 az -90 roll 0, 100 px per unit (render_match.py; a gauge for the fitted net), the Surfaces row the same view shifted by (-16.1, -2.6) px; against the Surfaces panel: silhouette IoU 0.835, blue-visible IoU 0.428, orange-visible IoU 0.008 (previous wave graph under its own best-fitting camera: silhouette IoU 0.803, blue 0.000, orange 0.382)
guessed: bi-degree orange (2, 5), blue (4, 6), polynomial (not stated in the paper); the ribbon is a control net fitted to one view, so its depth is not measured (the fairest net consistent with the image); not reproduced: the paper's alternation of the visible sheet (orange on the wall and the crest, blue in the trough and the lower-right part) needs folds in depth that one view does not pin down, ours shows the blue almost everywhere; the paper's end curls are flatter here; the offset field V and the separation k are our choices
paper_other_methods: paper: the open-source kernel returned three of the six edges only
truth_method: closed form (iso-parameter curves of the orange), surfaces exact polynomial; absence of other intersections certified numerically
